title: Method for Determining the Melting Temperature of Hf-C-N Thin Films Synthesized by Magnetron Deposition
content: The aim of this study was to develop a technology for the magnetron synthesis of hafnium carbonitride coatings and to develop a method for determining the melting temperature of the synthesized coating material that correlates with the melting temperatures of the corresponding bulk materials. Using magnetron sputtering, a coating with a composition of 53 at.% Hf, 27 at.% C, and 20 at.% N was obtained. X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy studies were performed to characterize the synthesized coatings. The results demonstrated the feasibility of magnetron synthesis of hafnium carbonitride coatings with a specified stoichiometric composition. The nitrogen concentration in the plasma-forming gas required for the onset of Hf–C–N compound formation was determined. A method for determining the melting temperature of thin-film coatings was developed, providing an approach for determining the melting temperatures of new materials in thin-film form.
